Subject: Pilot decision checklist + pricing scenarios for Umbra Health

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can put together the precise cost scenarios you asked for.

Recap of needs (what I heard)
- Production footprint: goal to support patient-facing inference for triage and note summarization, ramping over 3 months.
- Expected steady-state: ~18k generated tokens / day (~540k/mo). Peak bursts: up to 30 QPS sustained during clinic hours, short spikes to ~120 concurrent requests.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for single-turn generation.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + encrypted at rest; may need VPC options for the initial contract.

Decision axes we recommend you consider
1) Hosted API (utility/per-token): fastest to start, pay-as-you-go, easiest to iterate. Good if you want minimal ops and to try multiple models.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved commits): predictable throughput and cost with an appliance-like pool. Better if you have steady QPS and need lower per-token unit costs.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): required when you need full network isolation and customer-managed KMS. Higher setup overhead and usually a committed contract.

What we need from you to produce three side-by-side scenarios (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):
- Typical request size (avg tokens in + avg tokens generated) — if you don’t have exacts, a distribution (short/medium/long) works.
- Expected QPS profile: baseline and peak windows (hours/day).
- Region preference (we measured in us-west/us-east/eu-central).
- Any hard requirements around data residency or KMS.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-matrix.xlsx (simple matrix of capabilities) — I also attached a small CSV template (umbra-prod-profile.csv) you can fill with your token/QPS estimates.

Next steps
- If you can drop the CSV back to me by EOD Monday I’ll put together three quantitative scenarios with ballpark costs and expected latencies.
- I’ll loop in Rishi from pricing to run the reserved-commit math and give an apples-to-apples monthly cost comparison.

Proposed 30-min follow-up: Tue 3/14 10:00am PT (optional) — please let me know availability.

Thanks —
Marissa

- Typical commit sizes: Dedicated commitments are expressed as GPU-pool equivalents. For a workload like yours (baseline ~8 QPS, peak 28), common starting commits are 1–2 V100-equivalent GPUs for pilot (monthly), with the option to add burst capacity. I’ll ask Rishi for specific $ ranges.
- Token accounting: we provide baked-in batching and KV prefix caching. For short requests (12+80 average) batching improves throughput but only a small token efficiency improvement; caching can reduce repeated prompt cost if you have stable prefixes. Rishi will show real examples against your CSV.
- Private lead time: typical VPC peering + initial config is ~3–4 weeks; on-prem involves longer provisioning (6–10 weeks) and an onboarding fee. We’ll include those ranges.

I’ll schedule Tue 3/14 10:00am PT for a 30-min sync if that works — tentatively booked. If not, suggest an alternate time.

Hi Lydia / Marissa — looping in the cost scenarios; see the quick math below and the attached CSV with line-by-line assumptions (umbra-cost-scenarios.csv). I kept numbers conservative for planning.

Assumptions (from Lydia’s CSV): avg tokens out 80, avg tokens in 12, monthly generated tokens 500k (pilot), baseline QPS 8, peak sustained 28 QPS, spikes to 110 concurrency.

1) Hosted (per-token utility) — good for short pilot
- List per-generated-token price (approx): $0.0007 / generated token (includes compute & infra).
- Monthly cost (500k tokens): 500,000 * $0.0007 = $350/month.
- Peak handling: autoscaling covers burst but request-level latency may vary during spikes; no commitment needed.

2) Dedicated (monthly reserved commit) — best for predictable throughput
- Example starting commit: 1 GPU-equivalent pool (NVIDIA A10-equivalent) — $6,500/mo (including management/obs). This sustains ~60 QPS for short generations.
- For Umbra’s peak profile (sustained 28 QPS) 1 GPU gives headroom; if you want consistent p95 < 400ms during peaks, we’d recommend 1.5 GPU-equivalents (~$9,500/mo) to reduce queuing.
- Unit economics: at 500k tokens/mo, implied per-token cost on $6.5k commit = $0.013/token (but again you get consistent latency and predictable capacity). If you scale to 2M tokens, the per-token equivalent drops substantially.

3) Private / VPC (one-time onboarding + commit)
- Onboarding fee: $25k (one-time) + implementation (approx 40–80 engineer-hrs).
- Monthly baseline similar to Dedicated but add base infra & support fee (~$1k–$2k/mo). Lead time 3–6 weeks for VPC peering; on-prem longer.

Notes on caching & batching
- Effective token spend can be reduced via KV prefix caching for repeated prompts (we model this in the CSV). Batching improves throughput not token unit price significantly for mostly short responses.

Recommendation (short):
- If you want to validate product-market fit with low friction: start Hosted for 1 month to validate flows (~$350/mo) then transition to Dedicated commit once traffic stabilizes (1–2 GPUs).
- If security/compliance or procurement timeline forces it, we can fast-track Dedicated + VPC peering; I included onboarding and lead-time numbers above.

Attaching: umbra-cost-scenarios.csv (CSV with line-by-line math)

Happy to run a live model in the follow-up call Tue 3/14 10:00am PT.

—Rishi
